## `bam::Status`

[source](bam.goose#L15-L15)

```goose
enum Status { Record, End, Invalid, Truncated, IoError, Closed, TooLarge, Unsorted }
```

Record means a complete validated alignment; End is normal EOF. All other
statuses are sticky failures until open/seek. TooLarge is a configured size limit.
Unsorted is returned by pileup loading, not the sequential reader.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Closed);
```

## `bam::Reference`

[source](bam.goose#L27-L27)

```goose
struct Reference { name: i64, name_len: i64, length: i64 }
```

Reference name location in Reader.names and its declared length.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let ref = reader.references[0];
assert(reader.names[ref.name..ref.name + ref.name_len] == "chrA");
assert(ref.length == 200000);
```

<a id="api-3"></a>

## `bam::Fields`

[source](bam.goose#L43-L48)

```goose
struct Fields {
    tid:      i32, pos: i64, end: i64, reference_len: i64, flags: u16, mapq: u8,
    mate_tid: i32, mate_pos: i64, template_len: i32,
    name_len: i64, cigar: i64, cigar_len: i64, seq: i64, seq_len: i64,
    qual:     i64, aux: i64,
}
```

Parsed offsets are relative to the record's bytes, not the file. Use the
Record view's accessors rather than constructing this metadata yourself.
reference_len is the CIGAR reference span; end uses BAM's minimum span of 1.
tid/mate_tid and pos/mate_pos use -1 for missing references/positions.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let f = reader.record().fields;
assert(f.pos == 5 && f.end == 18 && f.reference_len == 13);
assert(f.seq_len == 13 && f.mate_tid == -1);
```

## `bam::Record`

[source](bam.goose#L61-L61)

```goose
struct Record { fields: Fields, bytes: const u8[:] }
```

A borrowed packed record. Reader views expire on the next read/seek/open/close.
Region stores expose a separate slab-backed pileup::Record view.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.name() == "match" && record.fields.tid == 0);
```

<a id="api-5"></a>

## `bam::Reader`

[source](bam.goose#L75-L88)

```goose
root struct Reader {
    stream:           bgzf::Reader,
    status:           Status         = Status.Closed,
    header:           u8[>..]        = [],
    names:            u8[>..]        = [],
    references:       Reference[>..] = [],
    bytes:            u8[>..]        = [],
    block_begin:      i64 = -1,
    fields:           Fields,
    data_start:       u64 = 0,
    max_record_bytes: i64 = 16777216,
    max_header_bytes: i64 = 16777216,
    max_references:   i64 = 1048576,
}
```

Owns stream, header, reference dictionary and a cross-block scratch buffer.
Records within one decoded BGZF block borrow that block without a copy.
Construct with Reader { .. }, then open. Do not mutate implementation fields.
Limits bound allocations from untrusted lengths and may be raised explicitly.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.references.len == 2);
assert(reader.header[..3] == "@HD");
```

## `bam::open`

[source](bam.goose#L138-L152)

```goose
fn open(reader: Reader&, path: const u8[:]) -> Status
```

Open and read the BAM header. Record means ready to read the first alignment;
it does not mean an alignment is already available. Failure closes the file.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.name() == "match");
```

<a id="api-8"></a>

## `bam::tell`

[source](bam.goose#L164-L164)

```goose
fn tell(reader: const Reader&) -> u64
```

Virtual offset of the next alignment, usable with seek on this same BAM.
The low 16 bits are the uncompressed position inside a compressed BGZF block.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let start = reader.tell();
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record && reader.tell() > start);
```

<a id="api-9"></a>

## `bam::seek`

[source](bam.goose#L181-L188)

```goose
fn seek(reader: Reader&, offset: u64) -> Status
```

Seek to an alignment boundary obtained from tell or a matching BAM index.
Invalidates record views and resets EOF/errors, retaining the header. An
arbitrary byte offset is not an alignment boundary and may fail on read.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let start = reader.tell();
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.seek(start) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.name() == "match");
```

## `bam::record`

[source](bam.goose#L252-L257)

```goose
fn record(reader: const Reader&) -> Record
```

Borrow the last successfully read record. Call only after read returns Record.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let first = reader.record();
assert(first.name() == "match");
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let second = reader.record();
assert(second.name() == "reverse"); // first's bytes are no longer valid.
```

<a id="api-12"></a>

## `bam::read`

[source](bam.goose#L273-L277)

```goose
fn read(reader: Reader&) -> Status
```

Read one alignment, reusing bytes. Record bytes are invalidated even when a
read fails. End and failures are sticky until open/seek. Records can span
many BGZF blocks.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
var count = 0;
var status = reader.read();
while status == bam::Status.Record { count += 1; status = reader.read(); }
assert(count == 21 && status == bam::Status.End);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.End);
```

## `bam::cigar`

[source](bam.goose#L472-L475)

```goose
fn cigar(record: const Record&, index: i64) -> u32
```

CIGAR word, with length in its upper 28 bits and SAM operation in its low 4.
index must be in [0, fields.cigar_len). Long-CIGAR CG arrays are transparent.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.cigar(0) == 13 << 4); // 13M
```

## `bam::base`

[source](bam.goose#L489-L494)

```goose
fn base(record: const Record&, index: i64) -> u8
```

Decode one packed base to its SAM IUPAC byte. Stored BAM orientation is kept;
reverse-strand records must not be reverse-complemented again for pileups.
index must be in [0, fields.seq_len).

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(record.base(0) == 'A' && record.base(1) == 'C');
```

<a id="api-19"></a>

## `bam_index::Index`

[source](bam_index.goose#L29-L35)

```goose
root struct Index {
    references: Reference[>..] = [], bins: Bin[>..] = [],
    chunks:     Chunk[>..]     = [], linear: u64[>..] = [],
    min_shift:  i64            = 14, depth: i64 = 5, csi: bool = false,
    status:     bam::Status    = bam::Status.Closed,
    max_bytes:  i64            = 268435456,
}
```

Owned, reusable BAI or CSI index. open accepts an explicit index path;
raw and BGZF-compressed indexes are supported. No file remains open.
max_bytes limits decompressed input (default 256 MiB), not total memory.
Treat fields other than max_bytes as read-only. CSI depth is 0..10 (u32
bin IDs), with min_shift + 3*depth <= 62. BAI covers coordinates below 2^29.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(index.references.len == 2);
```

<a id="api-20"></a>

## `bam_index::open`

[source](bam_index.goose#L76-L83)

```goose
fn open(index: Index&, path: const u8[:]) -> bam::Status
```

Replace the index. Failure clears any previous data; errors use bam::Status.
The index must belong to the BAM used for loading; the formats have no file
identity checksum, so a stale index cannot always be detected.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
assert(index.open("") == bam::Status.IoError);
assert(index.references.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-21"></a>

## `bam_index::query`

[source](bam_index.goose#L196-L245)

```goose
fn query(index: const Index&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64, output: Chunk[>..]&) -> bam::Status
```

Replace output with sorted, merged candidate chunks for [begin, end).
Candidates still require BAM overlap/filter checks. Empty regions succeed
with no chunks; invalid references or out-of-range coordinates fail.

```goose
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
var chunks: bam_index::Chunk[>..] = [];
assert(index.query(0, 5, 7, chunks) == bam::Status.Record && chunks.len > 0);
assert(index.query(0, 7, 7, chunks) == bam::Status.Record && chunks.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-22"></a>

## `pileup::Filter`

[source](pileup.goose#L20-L20)

```goose
struct Filter { exclude_flags: u16 = 0x704, min_mapq: u8 = 0, retain_zero_span: bool = false }
```

Read-level filters. Defaults exclude unmapped, secondary, QC-failed and
duplicate reads (0x704), but keep supplementary alignments. No base-quality
filtering or mate-overlap adjustment is applied to raw columns.
Unmapped and zero-reference-span records never produce columns, for any mask.
retain_zero_span keeps mapped zero-span records in input order in the store
for callers implementing read-admission policies; it defaults to false.

```goose
let filter = pileup::Filter { min_mapq: 20, .. };
assert(filter.exclude_flags == 0x704 && filter.min_mapq == 20);
```

<a id="api-23"></a>

## `pileup::SlimRecord`

[source](pileup.goose#L34-L41)

```goose
struct SlimRecord {
    tid:      i32, pos: i64, end: i64, reference_len: i64, flags: u16, mapq: u8,
    mate_tid: i32, mate_pos: i64, template_len: i32,
    name:     u32, name_len: u32, cigar: u32, cigar_len: u32,
    seq:      u32, seq_len: u32, qual: u32, aux: u32, aux_len: u32,
    // Store index of the linked mate; -1 when absent or ineligible.
    mate_index: i64 = -1,
}
```

Fixed-size metadata with offsets into Store's separate slabs. Coordinates
remain zero-based and half-open; slab offsets and lengths are element counts
(CIGAR elements are u32 words). Long CIGAR lengths are not limited to u16.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.records[0].pos == 5 && store.records[0].seq_len == 13);
```

<a id="api-24"></a>

## `pileup::Store`

[source](pileup.goose#L62-L74)

```goose
root struct Store {
    records:    SlimRecord[>..] = [],
    names:      u8[>..]         = [],
    bases:      u8[>..]         = [],
    cigars:     u32[>..]        = [],
    qualities:  u8[>..]         = [],
    auxiliary:  u8[>..]         = [],
    mate_stats: MateLinkStats   = MateLinkStats { .. },
    tid:        i32             = -1,
    begin:      i64             = 0,
    end:        i64             = 0,
    max_bytes:  i64             = 268435456,
}
```

Seqair-style region storage: metadata, names, unpacked IUPAC codes (0..15),
CIGAR words, qualities and raw auxiliary bytes each have their own slab.
Decode accepted reads once at load time; no packed BAM copy is retained.
max_bytes limits the sum of slab payload bytes, not metadata or capacity.
The payload is also limited to 2^32-1 bytes to bound the u32 slab offsets.
Exceeding either limit fails the load. Header data stays with the reader.
Treat all fields except max_bytes as read-only after load.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.records.len == 1);
reader.close(); // Stored records own their bytes, independently of Reader.
let record = store.record(0);
assert(record.name() == "match");
```

<a id="api-25"></a>

## `pileup::Record`

[source](pileup.goose#L89-L93)

```goose
struct Record {
    fields:        SlimRecord,
    name_bytes:    const u8[:], bases: const u8[:], cigar_words: const u32[:],
    quality_bytes: const u8[:], aux_bytes: const u8[:],
}
```

Borrowed slab-backed alignment, distinct from the reader's packed bam::Record.
Views survive reader close, but expire on the next load or slab mutation.
Accessors keep the same name/base/quality/CIGAR/aux semantics as bam::Record.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
let record = store.record(0);
assert(record.fields.seq_len == record.bases.len);
```

```goose
let record = store.record(0);
assert(record.quality(1) == 20);
```

<a id="api-32"></a>

## `pileup::MateLinkStats`

[source](pileup.goose#L204-L204)

```goose
struct MateLinkStats { pairs: i64 = 0, ambiguous_qnames: i64 = 0 }
```

Results of Seqair-style mate linking. pairs counts reciprocal links;
ambiguous_qnames counts eligible records without a free reciprocal partner
when another eligible record of that name was already seen. It is a record
count, not a count of distinct names. Inspect nonzero ambiguity explicitly.

```goose
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
let stats = store.link_mates();
assert(stats.pairs == 0 && stats.ambiguous_qnames == 0);
```

<a id="api-33"></a>

## `pileup::link_mates`

[source](pileup.goose#L221-L257)

```goose
fn link_mates(store: Store&) -> MateLinkStats
```

Link primary mapped pairs already in the store, using equal name bytes,
same-reference mate fields and reciprocal positions (not READ1/READ2 bits).
Secondary/supplementary, unmapped/mate-unmapped and empty-name records are
excluded. No outside-region mate fetch or overlap correction is performed.
Both load paths call this once after loading. Calling again is idempotent;
reordering/removing records requires relinking before reading mate_index.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.link_mates().pairs == 0 && store.records[0].mate_index == -1);
```

<a id="api-34"></a>

## `pileup::load`

[source](pileup.goose#L277-L293)

```goose
fn load<R>(store: Store&, reader: R&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64,
        filter: Filter = Filter { .. }) -> bam::Status
```

Scan from the reader's current position for [begin, end) on tid. Requires
coordinate-sorted input and a freshly opened reader for independent queries.
Returns Record on success, including an empty region. Error clears the store.
This is not an indexed query: it reads preceding records and consumes the
first mapped record beyond the region. Reopen before a different query.
Unsorted detects decreasing mapped coordinates only in the scanned prefix;
it cannot validate the unvisited remainder of a file. Empty regions do no I/O.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, reader.reference_id("chrA"), 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.records.len == 1);
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 9, 8) == bam::Status.Invalid);
assert(store.records.len == 0 && store.bases.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-35"></a>

## `pileup::load_indexed`

[source](pileup.goose#L327-L341)

```goose
fn load_indexed(store: Store&, reader: bam::Reader&, index: const bam_index::Index&,
                tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64, filter: Filter = Filter { .. }) -> bam::Status
```

Load [begin, end) via a matching BAI/CSI index and link retained mates.
Reuses the open reader, index and slab capacity across independent queries,
including backward queries and queries after EOF. No prefix scan or reopen.
Like Seqair, rejects non-overlapping/filtered raw records before full decode.
BGZF and record framing are always checked; names/auxiliary/query lengths
of discarded records are not validated. Retained records are fully checked.
Invalidates the reader's record view; call read before borrowing it again.
Failures clear the store. Sorting is checked only in visited chunks; indexes
cannot prove that the BAM is sorted, complete, or unchanged since indexing.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let index = bam_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("tests/data/example.bam.bai") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load_indexed(reader, index, 0, 95, 100) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(store.load_indexed(reader, index, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
{
    let record = store.record(0);
    assert(store.records.len == 1 && record.name() == "match");
}
assert(store.load_indexed(reader, index, 0, 0, 30,
    pileup::Filter { retain_zero_span: true, .. }) == bam::Status.Record);
var empty = 0;
for record in store.records { if record.reference_len == 0 { empty += 1; } }
assert(empty == 3); // Empty CIGAR, insertion-only, soft-clip-only.
store.columns() { pos, entries =>
    for entry in entries { assert(store.records[entry.record_index].reference_len > 0); }
};
```

<a id="api-37"></a>

## `pileup::Entry`

[source](pileup.goose#L481-L484)

```goose
struct Entry {
    record_index: i64, qpos: i64, base: u8, quality: u8,
    op:           Op, indel: i64,
}
```

record_index indexes Store.records. qpos is -1 for deletion/skip or absent
sequence; base is 'N' and quality 255 when unavailable. indel is anchored at
this column: positive for inserted bases after it, negative for a deletion.
Sequence remains in BAM's stored orientation, including reverse-strand reads.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 6) == bam::Status.Record);
store.columns() { pos, entries =>
    assert(pos == 5 && entries.len == 1);
    let e = entries[0];
    assert(e.qpos == 0 && e.base == 'A' && e.quality == 13);
    assert(e.op == pileup::Op.Base && e.indel == 0);
};
```

<a id="api-38"></a>

## `pileup::columns`

[source](pileup.goose#L565-L612)

```goose
fn columns<F: fn(i64, const Entry[:])>(store: const Store&)
```

Visit covered positions in [store.begin, store.end), in order. The callback
receives a zero-based position and a borrowed slice valid for that call only.
Column entries preserve input order. Scratch storage is reused; CIGAR cursors
only move forward. No reference FASTA, BAQ, mate dedup or depth cap is applied.
Only reference-consuming CIGAR operations produce entries; clips/insertions
alone never create columns. Empty positions are omitted, not zero-filled.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. };
defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(store.load(reader, 0, 5, 7) == bam::Status.Record);
var count = 0;
store.columns() { pos, entries =>
    assert(pos == 5 + count && entries.len == 1);
    count += 1;
};
assert(count == 2);
```

## `bam_encode::Alignment`

[source](bam_encode.goose#L26-L32)

```goose
struct Alignment {
    name: const u8[:] = "*",
    tid: i32 = -1, pos: i64 = -1, flags: u16 = 0, mapq: u8 = 0,
    mate_tid: i32 = -1, mate_pos: i64 = -1, template_len: i32 = 0,
    cigar: const u32[:] = EMPTY_CIGAR, sequence: const u8[:] = "",

```

Caller-owned alignment data. Sequence is ASCII IUPAC in stored orientation;
qualities are raw Phred bytes (empty means missing), CIGARs are native BAM
words, and aux contains raw BAM tags. -1 means absent reference/position.
No input is retained by encode or write. Empty sequence means absent SEQ.

```goose

let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { name: "read", tid: 0, pos: 4,
    cigar: cigar, sequence: "aN", .. };
var bytes: u8[>..] = [];

assert(bytes.len > 32);
```

[source](bam_encode.goose#L47-L52)

Encode a BAM payload (without block_size) into reusable caller storage.

Owns one output and its compressor. Construct with Writer { .. }, open,


Flush/finish, close the OS handle and release the compressor. Check the
result; deferred cleanup alone cannot report a failed final write. A poisoned
output is closed without an EOF marker. Repeated close succeeds.

```goose
    scratch_qualities: u8[>..] = [], scratch_aux: u8[>..] = [],
```

reference names live until open; records live until the next read/open/close.

## `cram::seek_slice`

[source](cram.goose#L422-L446)

```goose
fn seek_slice<R>(reader: Reader&, container_offset: i64, slice_offset: i64, size: i64, source: R&) -> bam::Status
```

Seek to and decode one CRAI slice. container_offset is an absolute file byte
offset; slice_offset is relative to container data, not its header. size must
match the landmark span. Header/reference metadata survives; borrowed records
do not. Reuses the compressed container when adjacent queries share it.
source has the same contract as read. Use cram_index::Cursor for region reads.

## `cram::read`

[source](cram.goose#L461-L488)

```goose
fn read<R>(reader: Reader&, source: R&) -> bam::Status
```

Read one record, reconstructing its entire slice before resolving mates.
source.fetch(name, begin, end, output) must replace output with exactly the
requested zero-based half-open reference window and return true on success.
An adapter can use goose-bio faidx::Reader; no FASTA dependency is imposed.
Reference bases are uppercased and nonzero single-reference MD5s checked.
Embedded/no-reference slices bypass source. Fetch failures and checked MD5
mismatches fail; multi-reference/zero-MD5 slices cannot verify FASTA identity.

```goose

let source = ExampleReference { .. };
assert(reader.read(source) == bam::Status.Closed);
```

## `cram::load`

[source](cram.goose#L517-L541)

```goose
fn load<R>(store: pileup::Store&, reader: Reader&, source: R&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64,
           filter: pileup::Filter = pileup::Filter { .. }) -> bam::Status
```

Load a region through the shared pileup engine, with a reference provider.
Requires sorted input and a freshly opened reader per independent query,
like the BAM/SAM sequential path. Errors clear the store; success links mates.

```goose
let reader = cram::Reader { .. };
let source = ExampleReference { .. };
let store = pileup::Store { .. };
assert(cram::load(store, reader, source, 0, 0, 10) == bam::Status.Invalid);
```

## `cram_index::Index`

[source](cram_index.goose#L22-L22)

```goose
root struct Index { entries: Entry[>..] = [], status: bam::Status = bam::Status.Closed, max_bytes: i64 = 268435456 }
```

Owned CRAI index. Plain text and concatenated gzip/BGZF members are accepted.
max_bytes bounds compressed and decoded index bytes separately, not total
allocations. No handle stays open. A CRAI has no file identity checksum.

```goose
let index = cram_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.status == bam::Status.Closed);
assert(index.open("") == bam::Status.IoError);
```

```goose
fn open(index: Index&, path: const u8[:]) -> bam::Status
```

Replace an index; errors clear the previous entries. Empty indexes are valid.

```goose
let index = cram_index::Index { .. };
assert(index.open("") == bam::Status.IoError && index.entries.len == 0);
```

<a id="api-64"></a>

## `cram_index::Cursor`

[source](cram_index.goose#L104-L108)

```goose
root struct Cursor {
    slices: Entry[>..] = [], at: i64 = 0, active: bool = false,
    tid: i32 = -1, begin: i64 = 0, end: i64 = 0,
    last_tid: i32 = -1, last_pos: i64 = -1, status: bam::Status = bam::Status.Closed,
}
```

Reusable per-worker region cursor. fetch replaces its selection; read returns
only overlapping records in physical slice/record order, including placed
unmapped records. Call reader.record() only after read returns Record. Do not
interleave cursors on the same reader. End/errors persist until fetch.

```goose
let cursor = cram_index::Cursor { .. };
assert(cursor.status == bam::Status.Closed);
```

<a id="api-65"></a>

## `cram_index::fetch`

[source](cram_index.goose#L119-L148)

```goose
fn fetch(cursor: Cursor&, index: const Index&, reader: cram::Reader&, tid: i32, begin: i64, end: i64) -> bam::Status
```

Select candidate slices for [begin,end). Nested spans are retained, duplicate
slice addresses removed, and selected slices sorted in file order. The caller
must use the index for this CRAM; skipped slices are not validated.

```goose
let cursor = cram_index::Cursor { .. }; let index = cram_index::Index { .. };
let reader = cram::Reader { .. };
assert(cursor.fetch(index, reader, 0, 0, 1) == bam::Status.Closed);
```


Decode only the selected slices, retaining the reader's reusable container
and codec storage. A fetch after EOF/error may seek backward or cross contigs.
Reference-provider semantics are the same as cram::read.

```goose
let cursor = cram_index::Cursor { .. }; let reader = cram::Reader { .. };
let source = ExampleReference { .. };
assert(cursor.read(reader, source) == bam::Status.Closed);
```

## `sam_writer::Writer`

[source](sam_writer.goose#L23-L29)

```goose
root struct Writer {
    output: io::BufferedWriter = io::BufferedWriter { file: io::FileHandle { fd: -1 }, used: 0, buffer: [] },
    status: bam::Status = bam::Status.Closed,
    references: bam::Reference[>..] = [], names: u8[>..] = [],
    line: u8[>..] = [], payload: u8[>..] = [],
```

Owns a plain SAM output and reusable buffers. Header/target names are copied
at open; input record views are never retained. Check close for write errors.
max_record_bytes bounds encoded BAM input; max_line_bytes bounds SAM output.

```goose
let writer = sam_writer::Writer { .. };
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
```

<a id="api-68"></a>

## `sam_writer::close`

[source](sam_writer.goose#L39-L45)

```goose
fn close(writer: Writer&) -> bam::Status
```

Flush and close. Errors poison writes until close/open; closing twice succeeds.
A failed output may contain complete earlier records, never a success signal.

```goose
let writer = sam_writer::Writer { .. };
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
```

<a id="api-69"></a>

## `sam_writer::open`

[source](sam_writer.goose#L95-L107)

```goose
fn open(writer: Writer&, path: const u8[:], header: const u8[:], refs: const bam::Reference[:], names: const u8[:]) -> bam::Status
```

Create/truncate plain SAM and write its header eagerly. Target IDs in records
must match this dictionary; they are not remapped. No output is opened until
header validation succeeds. Header text follows Seqair's SAM formatter.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. }; defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let writer = sam_writer::Writer { .. }; defer writer.close();
let path = "tests/data/writer.sam"; defer delete_file(path);
assert(writer.open(path, reader.header, reader.references, reader.names) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(writer.write(record) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
let input = sam::Reader { .. }; defer input.close();
assert(input.open(path) == bam::Status.Record && input.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let decoded = input.record();
assert(decoded.name() == "match");
```

## `sam_writer::write`

[source](sam_writer.goose#L191-L225)

```goose
fn write<T>(writer: Writer&, record: const T&) -> bam::Status
```

Format and buffer one validated BAM or slab record in stored orientation.
Long CIGARs are expanded and their first CG escape omitted. Aux order is
retained; integer tag widths become SAM i, floats follow Seqair/htslib's
six-significant-digit conventions. Invalid/oversized lines are not written.

```goose
let writer = sam_writer::Writer { .. };
let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { flags: 4, .. };
assert(writer.write(alignment) == bam::Status.Closed);
```


Serialize caller-owned alignment fields, validating through the BAM encoder.
Uses a reusable payload buffer; no borrowed field survives this call.

```goose
let writer = sam_writer::Writer { .. };
let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { name: "r", flags: 4, sequence: "ACN", .. };
assert(writer.write(alignment) == bam::Status.Closed);
```

## `cram_writer::Writer`

[source](cram_writer.goose#L32-L48)

```goose
root struct Writer {
    output: io::BufferedWriter = io::BufferedWriter { file: io::FileHandle { fd: -1 }, used: 0, buffer: [] },
    encoder: deflate::Compressor,
    status: bam::Status = bam::Status.Closed,
    references: i64 = 0, level: i32 = 6,
    records: i64 = 0, counter: i64 = 0, bases: i64 = 0, pending_bytes: i64 = 0,
    records_per_slice: i64 = 10000, max_slice_bytes: i64 = 67108864, max_record_bytes: i64 = 16777216,
    bf: u8[>..] = [], cf: u8[>..] = [], ri: u8[>..] = [], rl: u8[>..] = [], ap: u8[>..] = [], rg: u8[>..] = [],
    rn: u8[>..] = [], mf: u8[>..] = [], ns: u8[>..] = [], np: u8[>..] = [], ts: u8[>..] = [], tl: u8[>..] = [],
    fn_data: u8[>..] = [], fc: u8[>..] = [], fp: u8[>..] = [], dl: u8[>..] = [], mq: u8[>..] = [],
    ba: u8[>..] = [], qs: u8[>..] = [], in_data: u8[>..] = [], sc: u8[>..] = [], rs: u8[>..] = [],
    pd: u8[>..] = [], hc: u8[>..] = [], bb: u8[>..] = [], tag_data: u8[>..] = [],
    dictionary: u8[>..] = [], lines: TagLine[>..] = [], tags: u32[>..] = [],
    tag_line: u8[>..] = [], sequence: u8[>..] = [], payload: u8[>..] = [],
    header: u8[>..] = [], section: u8[>..] = [],
    container: u8[>..] = [], compressed: u8[>..] = [],
}
```

Owns a bounded, reference-free CRAM 3.0/3.1 output. Buffers one multi-reference
slice per container, with independent reusable data-series buffers, gzip/raw
blocks and detached mate fields. No reference fetching, sorting, lossy quality
reduction or index creation. Set limits before open; check close for errors.

```goose
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. };
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
```

[source](cram_writer.goose#L142-L179)

```goose
fn flush(writer: Writer&) -> bam::Status
```

Flush pending records into a complete container. Empty flush is a no-op.
It also flushes the I/O buffer (not fsync); failures poison subsequent writes.

```goose
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. };
assert(writer.flush() == bam::Status.Closed);
```

<a id="api-74"></a>

## `cram_writer::close`

[source](cram_writer.goose#L189-L202)

```goose
fn close(writer: Writer&) -> bam::Status
```

Flush records and append the canonical 38-byte CRAM EOF container only on
success. Always release the compressor/file. Repeated close succeeds.

```goose
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. };
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
```

<a id="api-75"></a>

## `cram_writer::open`

[source](cram_writer.goose#L224-L261)

```goose
fn open(writer: Writer&, path: const u8[:], header: const u8[:], refs: const bam::Reference[:], names: const u8[:], level: i32 = 6, minor_version: i32 = 1) -> bam::Status
```

Create/truncate CRAM, writing the definition and SAM-header container eagerly.
level 0 emits raw blocks; 1..12 use libdeflate gzip when smaller. minor_version
is 0 or 1 (default 1). Header SQ names/lengths must match the target dictionary.

```goose
let reader = bam::Reader { .. }; defer reader.close();
assert(reader.open("tests/data/example.bam") == bam::Status.Record);
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. }; defer writer.close();
let path = "tests/data/writer.cram"; defer delete_file(path);
assert(writer.open(path, reader.header, reader.references, reader.names) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(reader.read() == bam::Status.Record);
let record = reader.record();
assert(writer.write(record) == bam::Status.Record);
assert(writer.close() == bam::Status.Record);
let input = cram::Reader { .. }; defer input.close();
let reference = ExampleReference {};
assert(input.open(path) == bam::Status.Record && input.read(reference) == bam::Status.Record);
let decoded = input.record();
assert(decoded.name() == "match");
```

<a id="api-76"></a>

## `cram_writer::write`

[source](cram_writer.goose#L302-L365)

```goose
fn write<T>(writer: Writer&, record: const T&) -> bam::Status
```

Encode a validated BAM/slab record. CIGAR =/X normalize to M and adjacent
equal operations coalesce, as CRAM decoders do. Names, bases, qualities, tags
and detached mate fields are retained. Unsupported inputs (including mapped
records without a usable CIGAR, unmapped CIGAR/nonzero MAPQ, cF/d tags and
unpaired records carrying a mate target) fail instead of silently losing data.

```goose
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. };
let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { flags: 4, .. };
assert(writer.write(alignment) == bam::Status.Closed);
```


Validate and encode caller-owned fields using reusable BAM scratch storage.

```goose
let writer = cram_writer::Writer { .. };
let alignment = bam_encode::Alignment { name: "r", flags: 4, sequence: "ACN", .. };
assert(writer.write(alignment) == bam::Status.Closed);
```
